_doc: Journeys J1-J11 as route-level walks of the REAL console (rsi/runtime/ux/walk.mjs). `steps` are declarative: goto <path> | click <text-regex or css> | gone <css> | focus <css> | fill <css> <text> | hover <text-regex or css> | key <chord> | place <picker-css> | enabled <text-regex or css> | send <text-regex or css> | wait text=<literal> | wait css=<selector> | count text=<literal>|<css> <n> | url <regex> | value <css> <string> | shot <name> | vp <name>. `vp` scopes the steps that follow to one viewport (`["vp",""]` clears it): J2's rerun leg sends the fake's one-shot `[seed] shift` / `[seed] rewrite`, which write once per seed root, so replaying the leg at an earlier width would hand the next width a file it already changed. The seeded conversation already carries the seed's own answer plus one reply per width's tray send, so the rerun leg's reply waits are indexed past them (`nth=2` at the leg start, `nth=3` after `[seed] shift`, `nth=4` after `[seed] rewrite`); a lower index is satisfied before the round it exists to gate.  Selectors are best-effort (zh+en); a Playwright selector chain such as `css=.kin-diff-comment-glyph >> nth=4` picks the glyph on the seeded line. A selector prefixed with `?` is optional (empty-daemon / missing seed) and is recorded as skipped; any other missing or failed action is a hard failure. `focus` exists for a trigger inside a composer: the field blurs, the page re-lays-out, and a mouse click lands on the wrapper; focus then `key Enter` is the accessible path and the stable one. `place` opens the working-directory picker, chooses a listed place or a project root the daemon reports, and records `<journey>-<vp>-skipped-no-workdir` (a skip, not a failure) when there is genuinely nothing to choose. `gone <css>` waits (RSI_UX_WAIT_MS, default 15000) until no visible match of the selector remains and is a hard failure when one is still on screen at the deadline; it proves a decision landed and took its control off the screen. `enabled` asserts a control is usable without pressing it (a throwaway daemon has no fake agent, so starting a run would launch a real CLI); a disabled control is a hard failure unless the page names the missing prerequisite on screen. `send` is the press itself: it keeps that disabled verdict, then asks the daemon's /api/agents whether the claude-code binary lives under a directory named journeys_fake_agent (the seed's own test), records `<journey>-<vp>-skipped-no-fake-agent` with the reason and never clicks when it does not, and only then clicks and waits for /tasks/<id>. A walk must never launch a real CLI. `wait` waits until that literal text / selector is VISIBLE (timeout RSI_UX_WAIT_MS, default 15000; a third element overrides it for that step in ms, e.g. `["wait","text=…","20000"]`, because the fake holds the first round open; a timeout is a hard failure). `count` asserts how many VISIBLE matches of a `text=`/`css=` needle are on screen at that instant — it does not wait — and is a hard failure when the number differs; J3 uses `count text=<the reply> 0` before the reply wait to prove the mid-run follow-up was read before the first answer. `url` waits until the current pathname matches the regex. `value` asserts an input's current value. `node css=<selector> <name>` tags the matched element with `data-kin-walk-node=<name>` on its first call and, on every later call with the same name, asserts it is the SAME element (a remount fails with `the <name> node was replaced`). `scroll css=<selector> <px>|bottom` puts a scroller where the reader left it; `scroll-kept css=<selector> <px>` asserts it came back within 48px, waiting for the pane's layout-effect restore. J9 is the Mac switch proof: it opens a seeded conversation, scrolls it, tags the shell, types an unsent draft, switches conversations and areas, and reads the shell identity, the scroll position and the draft back. J11 is the phone switch proof: it leaves the conversation for the list with `back`, opens another, comes back and reads the same three back, then leaves again, walks the footer's routines and sessions entries, and reopens the conversation to read the draft and the position a second time — the pane was off screen, so the return proves the restore, not only the element's identity. `paths` maps changed files to the journeys they can affect (first match wins; no match = all journeys). `viewports` are WxH. J8 is the phone review loop and is phone-only: its `click` is a pointer press (Playwright's mouse) on the changed line's glyph by index, so it proves the hit target and layout at 390 — not touch-event synthesis. J7 reopens the seeded conversation after Back by pointer tap (`click [data-session-row="{conversation}"]`), so a surface covering the row reddens the walk; the keyboard path would hide that dead zone.
